name: Thai Thai San Marcos
blocked: Both first-party domains dead (thaithaisanmarcosrestaurant.com and thaithaisanmarcos.com both 404/unpublished, confirmed by curl -sIL). DoorDash marketplace (address-verified: 801 South Twin Oaks Valley Road, San Marcos) has schema.org Menu JSON-LD with 91 items, but the entire core of the menu -- every noodle dish (Pad Thai, Pad See-Ewe, Chow Mein, etc.), every curry, and every wok entree, 37 items total -- carries an empty offers.price because they are protein-choice build-your-own dishes priced only inside a modifier selector that DoorDash does not expose in server-rendered HTML or JSON-LD. The 54 items that DO carry a price (appetizers, salads, soups, fried rice, specialties) look implausibly high for a strip-mall Thai restaurant (Orange Chicken $28.60, fried rice dishes $39.35, Hot Pot Noodle $48.30) -- roughly 2-3x what this cuisine/setting normally runs, with no clean divisor found (not 1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25/1.3). Could not confirm whether this is a genuine price level or a DoorDash-side markup/portion-size artifact without a second source. A WebSearch summary suggested Pad Thai/Yellow Curry around $17.45 each, but that was never verified on an actual page (WebSearch summaries are not sources per playbook) so it is not used. Needs: a browser to open the protein-choice modifier modals on DoorDash (or Uber Eats, which 403'd curl with a bot challenge) to get real base prices, and ideally a working first-party or POS source to validate the high fixed-item prices before trusting them.
notes: Categories reached: Most Ordered, Appetizer & Salad, Soups, Noodles, Fried Rice, Curry, Entrees, Specialties (all present in the DD JSON-LD section list, so shape is complete) but prices are unusable for the majority of core dishes.

name: Tabu Shabu
notes: First-party site (tabushabusandiego.com/menu, address on page confirmed 3647 30TH ST, San Diego, CA 92104, matching work list). Menu is a Next.js RSC-streamed page with no plain HTML prices; extracted by reconstructing the full React Server Component payload from self.__next_f.push() chunks (resolving all "$Lxx" forward references into their source segments) then reading the resulting name/description/price tree. Protein items are priced per portion size (menu legend: '4oz reg · 6oz lg · 8oz dbl · 3oz side'); each size is recorded as a separate dish since each is a real distinct price. Broth/noodle upgrades (Sukiyaki, Tonkotsu, Ramen noodle, Kale ramen noodle) are recorded at their stated upcharge. Included no-charge items (Traditional kombu, Miso broth, White/brown rice, Udon, Shirataki, Craft beer, 'Save your noodles', Hot tea) were dropped -- they carry no per-item price, they are bundled into the hot-pot base price. Categories reached: Step 1 Broth, Step 2&3 Rice+Noodle, Step 4 Pick Your Protein, Tabu Exclusive Premium Proteins, Step 5 Finish, Starters, Extras & Garnishes, Sake, Beer & Wine, Zero-Proof, Dessert -- this is the restaurant's full published menu, no sections held back.

name: Valle
notes: First-party site (address on page confirmed 222 North Pacific Street, matching work list). Valle is a fixed-tasting-menu fine-dining restaurant (Michelin-starred). The site's own schema.org Menu JSON-LD confirms this is a real gap, not a capture failure: the Tasting Menu and Menu Breve blocks price the whole menu (not per-course), and the El Sillon Bar, Bar Menu and Cocktails JSON-LD blocks list every dish/drink name and description but every 'offers' field is either absent or an empty {"@type":"Offer"} with no price key -- confirmed by reading the raw JSON-LD, not just the rendered page. So per-item a la carte and cocktail prices are not published anywhere on the restaurant's own site. Categories reached: Tasting Menu (priced), Menu Breve (priced), El Sillon Bar Experience (reached, genuinely unpriced), Bar Menu (reached, genuinely unpriced -- 14 items: Bean Bread, Sikil Pak, Ceviche Verde Tostada, Trucha Tom Kha, Half Dozen Baja Oysters, Not Cesar, Burrito, THE Cheeseburger, Quesataco, Birria, Pescado, Arroz con Leche, Ice Cream, Legoland flan), Cocktails (reached, genuinely unpriced -- 7 drinks: Milpa, Fogata, Malinche, Polanco, Rum-Cha-Cha, Sandy, Maggie). Recorded the tasting-menu tiers and supplements as the priced 'dishes' since that is the restaurant's actual per-order pricing structure; course lists are folded into each menu's description.

name: Barra Oliva
blocked: First-party site (barraoliba.com, address confirmed 1980 Kettner Blvd #30, San Diego, CA 92101, matching work list) renders the complete menu -- Happy Hour, Gildas, Charcuteria & Cheeses, Tapas Frias, Hot Tapas, Raw Seafood, Starters, Rice Dishes, Meat & Fish, Sides -- with full dish names and descriptions, but every base-price element (<div class="mb-5">) is empty in the server-rendered HTML; only add-on upcharges render (e.g. 'add jamon serrano or boquerones +$6', 'add jamon iberico 5Js +$17'). Confirmed this is a real gap and not a stripped-tag miss by grepping the raw HTML directly around several items (Croquetas of the day, Galician style EVOO potato chips) and finding the price div genuinely empty; there is no 'dish-price' CSS class anywhere in the page. Fetched the site's one custom JS bundle (/build/assets/app-f6e5ee3d.js, 255KB) and found zero references to 'price' in it, so this does not look like a client-side-injected price the JS would fill in from an API -- but a browser render was not possible to fully rule that out. WebSearch/press coverage confirms a $9-$30 range exists in reality but no source gives per-dish numbers. Needs a browser to load the live page and confirm whether prices appear after JS executes (possibly via a request this static fetch can't trigger), or a photographed/PDF menu.
notes: Categories reached: Happy Hour, Gildas, Charcuteria & Cheeses, Tapas Frias, Hot Tapas, Raw Seafood, Starters, Rice Dishes, Meat & Fish, Sides -- full section list read from the site, all dish names/descriptions captured, none priced.

name: AVANT Restaurant
notes: First-party site (avantrestaurant.com) embeds a SinglePlatform widget (data-location=/avant-17) rather than hosting menu HTML/PDF directly; resolved the widget's redirect chain to the live SinglePlatform page, which the site actively loads as its own 'Our Menu' content (not a third-party directory listing found independently). Address on the page confirmed 17550 Bernardo Oaks Dr, San Diego, CA 92128, matching work list. Parsed the page's embedded schema.org Restaurant/OfferCatalog JSON-LD (nested Menu > Section > Offer tree) for the bulk of items. Two known JSON-LD gaps were hand-patched from the page's own rendered text: (1) Seafood Tower only carried its 'Small' price ($85) in the JSON-LD -- the Large ($135) and both Supplemental Upcharge tiers ($50/$80) were read from the surrounding text and added; (2) the four private-event Bar Packages price per-person-per-hour in plain text inside the item name rather than in the JSON-LD price field ('$37 Per Person for (1) Hour; $23 Per Person for Each Additional Hour', etc.) -- split into First Hour / Each Additional Hour rows. Dropped items with no real price: the Garden/Market/Artisan private-dining prix-fixe course lists genuinely carry no per-person price anywhere on the page (private-event menus priced on inquiry). Categories reached and priced: AVANT Dinner Menu (Signature Prix Fixe, crudo, Beginnings, Land+Sea, Accompaniment, full wine-by-glass and cocktail lists), AVANT Bar Happy Hour Menu, Wines by Sommelier (bottle list), Bar Packages, Reception Hors D'Oeuvres & Canapes, AVANT Dessert Menu. Reached but unpriced: Garden/Market/Artisan private-event menus (no per-person price published). Prices look internally consistent (a clean, ascending fine-dining ladder with no repeating divisor pattern), consistent with genuine first-party pricing rather than a directory markup, but SinglePlatform listings are known to go stale, so confidence is medium rather than high.

name: Roger's Pizzerolo
notes: First-party site (Owner.com platform, x-powered-by: Owner.com header). Address on page confirmed 2990 Jamacha Rd #102, El Cajon, CA 92019, matching work list. Menu data is a schema.org Restaurant/Menu graph embedded as a JSON-encoded, HTML-entity-escaped string inside the page's Astro state blob (key "schema") rather than a plain <script type=application/ld+json> tag -- extracted by unescaping HTML entities then walking the backslash-escaped JSON string. Two menus exist under this location: a Catering menu (4 sections: Catering Appetizers, Catering Salads, Catering Subs, Catering -- bulk/party-tray items) and the regular menu (11 sections, 108 items). Recorded only the regular menu; catering/party-tray items were excluded as an adjunct per the playbook's own guidance. Categories reached: Specialty White Pizza, Pizza Pies, Specialty Pizza, Pizza Special, Calzone & Stromboli, Appetizers, Pasta, Sandwiches and Wraps, Salads, Side Orders, Desserts and Drinks -- this is the complete regular menu, no sections held back. Ran the markup divisor test: dividing by 1.04 lands 79% of the 108 prices exactly on a .99/.95-ending value (e.g. $29.11 -> $27.99, $20.79 -> $19.99), matching the playbook's documented pattern for a 4% online-ordering surcharge baked into a first-party storefront. Recorded the prices exactly as shown on the ordering page (what a customer is actually charged today ordering directly from the restaurant's own site) rather than backing out the 4% to guess an unlisted dine-in price, since no source states that lower number -- flagging the pattern here for transparency rather than inventing a corrected figure.
